report.source_text: Histopathologic examination revealed a dense predominantly plasmocytic infiltrate throughout the entire superficial dermis. The epidermis presented thickening and elongation of the rete ridges – which correspond to the clinical features of the disease – along with the presence of eosionophilic bodies and exocytosis of lymphocytes (Figure 2). We observed no signs of neoplasia or malignancy.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old woman presented with a lobulated warty lesion on the lower lip that first appeared during her first pregnancy 7 years ago and disappeared, then recurred during her second pregnancy 5 years later and progressively worsened. Physical examination described the lesion as lobulated and warty. Histopathology of the lesion biopsy showed dense predominantly plasmocytic infiltrate in the superficial dermis, thickening and elongation of rete ridges, presence of eosinophilic bodies, and lymphocyte exocytosis without malignancy. The patient was treated with three monthly triamcinolone acetonide injections, resulting in gradual lesion improvement with no recurrence over 6 months. No explicit documentation was found on differential diagnoses exclusion.
